title: Enforcement migration plan
subtitle: Reshaped 2026-11-04: the MVP records what the flip will record. Waves 1–4 are ledger-mvp.

plan.fact: Is this domain blocked from sending?

stages.stop: Today: the disabled flag is the only record; DisableDomainEvent says when, not why.
Ledger and readings tables exist and nothing writes them. Reverting leaves empty tables.
Every writer appends an event beside the flag. Disables from before this deploy have no case, so the ledger is incomplete, but nothing reads it yet.
Every pre-ledger disable has a legacy.unrecorded case. The ledger should now match the flags.
Drift is reported, never acted on. Stay here until it reads zero.
The ledger is the truth: commit writes the flag only from a before→after transition. The old queue still reads DisableDomainEvent, which is still written.
Admins work open cases from the case table; DisableDomainEvent is still written and unread by the new queue.
The domain-wide re-enable and the disable-event queue are gone. DisableDomainEvent is still written (dropping it is an extra).

branches.name: add-enforcement-event-ledger
branches.does: Adds an append-only stream of enforcement decisions per team

branches.name: purge-a-teams-ledger-with-the-team
branches.does: Purges a team's enforcement events when the team is deleted

branches.name: fold-a-teams-enforcement-events
branches.does: Folds a team's enforcement events into its cases, each scoped to a team, domain or email

branches.name: record-enforcement-events
branches.does: Drafts case openings from a cause and appends them to a team's stream under its lock, opening nothing for a cause that already holds an open case

branches.name: record-domain-disables-on-the-ledger
branches.does: Opens a case on the ledger for every domain disable, with its reason, actor and the reading behind it

branches.name: create-domains-in-one-transaction
branches.does: Creates a sending domain, its disable event, its suspicious reading and its case in one transaction

branches.name: record-domain-reenables-on-the-ledger
branches.does: Releases every case holding a domain on the ledger when an admin re-enables it

branches.name: set-domain-disabled-flags
branches.does: Reads and sets a team's domain disabled flags and lists the teams with a disabled domain

branches.name: list-teams-on-the-ledger
branches.does: Lists every still-existing team with events on the enforcement ledger

branches.name: adopt-legacy-disables
branches.does: Adds a script that gives every domain disabled before the ledger a legacy case, once, before the ledger becomes the truth

branches.name: check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags
branches.does: Adds a read-only script that reports every domain whose disabled flag disagrees with the ledger's open cases

branches.name: find-the-readings-cases-point-at
branches.does: Finds a team's notices and suspicious activities by id, the readings a case can point at

branches.name: read-a-teams-open-cases
branches.does: Reads a team's open cases with the domain each holds and the readings it points at

branches.name: serve-a-teams-open-cases
branches.does: Serves a team's open cases to the admin panel

branches.name: list-open-cases-on-domain-review
branches.does: Lists a team's open cases above the domain assessment, with the readings each points at

branches.name: mark-a-reading-reviewed
branches.does: Find an email's unreviewed readings and mark readings reviewed, as the ledger's reviews project them

branches.name: review-readings-on-the-ledger
branches.does: Review readings that opened no case on the ledger, marking them reviewed in the same transaction

branches.name: detect-banned-words
branches.does: Find banned words in an email as a detector that returns a reading and writes nothing

branches.name: detect-phishing
branches.does: Tag an email with the phishing model as a detector that returns a reading and writes nothing

branches.name: record-content-readings
branches.does: Record every content detector's reading through one model, keeping the data the admin views read

branches.name: point-content-cases-at-their-reading
branches.does: Point every content case at the reading that opened it

branches.name: review-an-emails-readings-on-the-ledger
branches.does: Record every review of an email's readings on the ledger instead of setting the reviewed flag directly

branches.name: project-disabled-from-cases
branches.does: Records case events and writes a domain's disabled flag only where those events change whether a case holds it

branches.name: reenable-through-cases
branches.does: Re-enables a domain by releasing every case that holds it, letting the projection turn it on

branches.name: disable-domains-through-cases
branches.does: Turns a domain off by opening the case its cause calls for, so the flag follows the cases

branches.name: create-domains-under-cases
branches.does: Creates a domain through the cases, inserting it disabled when a team-wide case already holds its team

branches.name: release-a-case
branches.does: Releases one open case as a person with a reason, reinstating the team's provider tenant when that turns a domain back on

branches.name: serve-case-release
branches.does: Serves releasing one case to the admin panel

branches.name: release-cases-from-domain-review
branches.does: Adds a release button with a reason and note to each open case on domain review

branches.name: add-the-case-table
branches.does: Adds a table holding each case's current state, rebuildable from the ledger, with queries to write a case and list open ones

branches.name: project-cases-into-the-table
branches.does: Writes each case an enforcement commit or legacy adoption touches into the case table, in the same transaction

branches.name: rebuild-the-case-table
branches.does: Adds a script that rewrites every case in the table from the ledger

branches.name: list-domains-for-teams
branches.does: Lists the sending domains of several teams at once

branches.name: list-the-case-queue
branches.does: Lists open cases across teams, newest first, each with its team, the domain it holds and a domain to review

branches.name: serve-the-case-queue
branches.does: Serves the open case queue to the admin panel

branches.name: review-domains-by-id
branches.does: Lets domain review load by sending domain as well as by disable event

branches.name: queue-domains-by-open-cases
branches.does: Lists open cases in the disabled domains tab and reviews each by its domain

branches.name: stop-reenabling-domains-directly
branches.does: Removes the domain-wide re-enable, so a domain turns back on only by releasing its cases

branches.name: retire-the-disable-event-queue

transitions.gate: Wave 1 merged and deployed: add-enforcement-event-ledger, purge-a-teams-ledger-with-the-team, fold-a-teams-enforcement-events. Migrations pass squawk; the append-only trigger, the CHECKs and the payload-version CHECK are in.
transitions.rollback: Safe: the tables are empty and unread. Reverting the migration drops an empty table.

transitions.gate: The ledger table exists in prod and purge has deployed (record-disables carries an `after` edge on it, so a deleted team never leaves events behind). Wave 2 merges in order: record-enforcement-events → record-domain-disables → create-domains-in-one-transaction → record-domain-reenables, ideally one deploy.
transitions.rollback: Revert the wave-2 PRs: disables and re-enables go back to flag-only. Events already written stay valid (`v:1`) and just stop growing; adoption fills the gap later. The one risk is the reverse: a ledger write that throws rolls back its disable — every call site has a test building its cause the way production does, and notes fall back to fixed text so the person-writes-note CHECK can't fire.

transitions.gate: Wave 2 has been deployed long enough that no request still runs the old code (one deploy cycle). Wave 3 merged: set-domain-disabled-flags → list-teams-on-the-ledger → adopt-legacy-disables.
transitions.rollback: Safe: legacy cases sit unread while the flag is the truth.
transitions.manual: `npm run script-runner adoptLegacyDisables` (dry run: counts teams and domains), then `DRY_RUN=false npm run script-runner adoptLegacyDisables`. Run it AFTER wave 2 deploys, never before: a disable in between would get no case.

transitions.gate: Adoption ran for real; a second dry run reports 0 domains. check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags merged, and wave 4 (the domain-review panel) can ship now that every disabled domain has a case.
transitions.manual: `npm run script-runner checkLedgerAgreesWithFlags`, daily. Known expected drift: an admin re-enabling ONE domain of a team held by a team-wide case releases the team case while the team's other domains stay off with no case — the drift report names them, and they're exactly what the flip changes (post-flip that re-enable turns the whole team on).

transitions.gate: Drift reads **zero** on runs a week apart, apart from the named partial re-enables above, each reviewed. Content-detector branches merged (they ride between verify and flip and change no flag).
transitions.rollback: Safe: the old code writes the flag and records events exactly as at verify, and commit's flag writes agree with them. Cases released in the new UI stay released.

transitions.gate: The flip is stable: drift still zero after a day.
transitions.rollback: Safe: the old queue reads DisableDomainEvent, which is still written.
transitions.manual: `DRY_RUN=false npm run script-runner rebuildEnforcementCases` once project-cases-into-the-table deploys.

transitions.gate: No one uses the old queue or the domain-wide re-enable.
transitions.rollback: Code only: bring the route back. Nothing stored changed.

extras.name: Content readings & review
extras.detail: reading.reviewed, email scope and the publish effect. Already built into the core branches; the open question is whether the first PRs should show only the core schema.

extras.name: R1 · payload schema version
extras.why: The first event written in prod fixes the payload shape forever. Without a version, retiring a reason or adding a required field later means a lenient decoder for every old event.
extras.detail: **Done in the MVP.** `record` stamps `v: 1` on every payload; `parseEvent` reads `payloads[type][v]`; the database refuses a payload with no numeric `v` (`EnforcementEvent_data_names_its_version`). A stored version may widen but never narrow, so old streams always replay.

extras.name: R2 · cause keys
extras.why: Events written without a causal key can never be deduplicated against a redelivery; they need a 'no key' exception in perpetuity.
extras.detail:
A durable key from the source occurrence and policy, deduplicated across all history, separate from 'is a case already open'.

**Recommendation: leave it out and record `accepted`.** It's a real design change, and its cliff is softer than R1's: only events from before the key can't be deduplicated, which matters only if a provider resends an old notification after its case was released. Suggested reason: *pre-key events can't dedupe; redelivery window is short; the fix lands right after the flip.* If you'd rather carry no such window, press m on it too.
extras.accepted: Repeat causes already dedupe against open cases from day one (`unlessAlreadyOpen`: same scope, effect and reason), and team-wide causes open one team case. Only a provider redelivering an old notice after its case was released reopens it; a durable cause key can come later without touching stored events.

extras.name: R3 · required evidence + provider readings
extras.detail: Automated openings must cite an existing same-team reading; SES tenant notices become readings. Checked at write time, so it can tighten later.

extras.name: R5 · reading IDs in jobs
extras.detail: Review and publish jobs carry the reading IDs they decided on. Jobs drain, so this only changes code.

extras.name: R6 · condition cases
extras.detail: Deletion requested and provider tenant disabled close when the condition clears; needs the ledger as the authority.

extras.name: property.set (Unleash)
extras.detail: skipSafetyChecks as a policy input on the ledger. No type CHECK to widen; the legacy seed needs the rules_open_or_review exception.

extras.name: Drift monitor
extras.detail: **In the MVP as a script** (check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags, wave 3), run by hand daily during verify. A scheduled alert is the follow-up.

extras.name: Stop writing DisableDomainEvent
extras.detail: Once nothing reads it; the timeline shows old rows raw as pre-ledger history.

extras.name: Team timeline
extras.detail: Readings, events and pre-ledger DisableDomainEvent/AdminPanelInteraction rows in one view.

extras.name: Fold snapshots
extras.detail: The fold is O(events per team) per commit. Add snapshots when a team's stream passes a measured size, not before.

sections.title: The MVP in four waves
sections.body:
The rule: **the MVP records exactly what the post-flip code records for the same action**, so an event stored now means the same after the flip.

| wave | branches (merge in this order) | what changes in prod |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · inert | [add-enforcement-event-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/add-enforcement-event-ledger) · [purge-a-teams-ledger-with-the-team](canopy://v2/b/loops/purge-a-teams-ledger-with-the-team) · [fold-a-teams-enforcement-events](canopy://v2/b/loops/fold-a-teams-enforcement-events) | an empty table, code nobody calls |
| 2 · writes | [record-enforcement-events](canopy://v2/b/loops/record-enforcement-events) → [record-domain-disables-on-the-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/record-domain-disables-on-the-ledger) → [create-domains-in-one-transaction](canopy://v2/b/loops/create-domains-in-one-transaction) → [record-domain-reenables-on-the-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/record-domain-reenables-on-the-ledger) | every disable, creation and re-enable appends events in its own transaction; flags unchanged |
| 3 · backfill + drift | [set-domain-disabled-flags](canopy://v2/b/loops/set-domain-disabled-flags) → [list-teams-on-the-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/list-teams-on-the-ledger) → [adopt-legacy-disables](canopy://v2/b/loops/adopt-legacy-disables) → [check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags](canopy://v2/b/loops/check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags) | two scripts: adopt once, check daily |
| 4 · panel | [find-the-readings-cases-point-at](canopy://v2/b/loops/find-the-readings-cases-point-at) → [read-a-teams-open-cases](canopy://v2/b/loops/read-a-teams-open-cases) → [serve-a-teams-open-cases](canopy://v2/b/loops/serve-a-teams-open-cases) → [list-open-cases-on-domain-review](canopy://v2/b/loops/list-open-cases-on-domain-review) | admins see each open case, its reason, who opened it and the reading behind it |

Forest: [ledger-mvp](canopy://v2/p/loops/ledger-mvp). The grid's **t** pages hold each gate, manual step and rollback.

**Gates (2026-11-04, 23:30):** all 15 branches are gates-green and server-recorded on their current trees, waves 1–4. Nothing is pushed: start with wave 1, bottom-up, PR titles and bases on the PRs page.

sections.title: PR titles and bodies
sections.body:
Titles are `feat(loo-6239): <title>`. Each base is the branch above it ("Stacked on: #N" once that PR exists). Bodies are the why, above the Traffic Cop template.

**1 · [add-enforcement-event-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/add-enforcement-event-ledger)** · base `main`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): add the enforcement ledger`
- body: an insert-only stream of enforcement decisions per team, numbered per team so writers take turns under an advisory lock. the database refuses edits, actorless events, a person without a note, and a payload that doesn't name its version.

**1 · [purge-a-teams-ledger-with-the-team](canopy://v2/b/loops/purge-a-teams-ledger-with-the-team)** · base `add-enforcement-event-ledger`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): purge a team's ledger with the team`
- body: team deletion removes everything else the team owns, so for now its enforcement history goes too. an explicit delete, not a cascade, so keeping history later is one line. merge before record-every-domain-disable.

**1 · [fold-a-teams-enforcement-events](canopy://v2/b/loops/fold-a-teams-enforcement-events)** · base `add-enforcement-event-ledger`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): fold a team's enforcement events`
- body: a pure apply turns a team's stream into its cases. every opening says what it covers, what it stops and which readings tripped it, and each payload is read at the version it was written.

**2 · [record-enforcement-events](canopy://v2/b/loops/record-enforcement-events)** · base `fold-a-teams-enforcement-events`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): record drafted enforcement events`
- body: writers draft their events against the stream as it stands under the team lock, so a repeated cause opens nothing and every payload is stamped with its version.

**2 · [record-domain-disables-on-the-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/record-domain-disables-on-the-ledger)** · base `record-enforcement-events`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): record every domain disable`
- body: every disable opens the case its cause calls for in the same transaction: a domain case, or one team case for a team-wide disable. the flag and disable event are written exactly as before.

**2 · [create-domains-in-one-transaction](canopy://v2/b/loops/create-domains-in-one-transaction)** · base `record-domain-disables-on-the-ledger`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): create domains in one transaction`
- body: a suspicious new domain used to land in four separate writes, so a crash between them could leave it disabled with no reading or case. now they commit together.

**2 · [record-domain-reenables-on-the-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/record-domain-reenables-on-the-ledger)** · base `create-domains-in-one-transaction`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): record domain re-enables`
- body: a re-enable releases every case holding the domain as the admin who did it, team-wide ones included: the same release the ledger will make once it decides.

**3 · [set-domain-disabled-flags](canopy://v2/b/loops/set-domain-disabled-flags)** · base `record-domain-reenables-on-the-ledger`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): set domain disabled flags`
- body: the adoption and drift scripts need each team's disabled domains and the teams that have any.

**3 · [list-teams-on-the-ledger](canopy://v2/b/loops/list-teams-on-the-ledger)** · base `set-domain-disabled-flags`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): list teams on the ledger`
- body: the drift check walks every team with events, not just the ones with a disabled domain.

**3 · [adopt-legacy-disables](canopy://v2/b/loops/adopt-legacy-disables)** · base `list-teams-on-the-ledger`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): adopt legacy disables`
- body: domains disabled before the ledger have no case. this gives each one a legacy case once, as a script, after every writer records.

**3 · [check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags](canopy://v2/b/loops/check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags)** · base `adopt-legacy-disables`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): check the ledger agrees with the flags`
- body: before the ledger becomes the truth for disabled, prove it agrees with the flags we trust today. after the flip the same check catches drift.

**4 · [find-the-readings-cases-point-at](canopy://v2/b/loops/find-the-readings-cases-point-at)** · base `check-the-ledger-agrees-with-the-flags`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): find a team's readings by id`
- body: a case points at the notice or suspicious activity that tripped it; these read them back, scoped to the team.

**4 · [read-a-teams-open-cases](canopy://v2/b/loops/read-a-teams-open-cases)** · base `find-the-readings-cases-point-at`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): read a team's open cases`
- body: folds the team's stream and joins each open case to its domain and readings, so a reviewer sees why without the ledger copying any reading.

**4 · [serve-a-teams-open-cases](canopy://v2/b/loops/serve-a-teams-open-cases)** · base `read-a-teams-open-cases`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): serve a team's open cases`
- body: a thin admin read over the model, for the review panel.

**4 · [list-open-cases-on-domain-review](canopy://v2/b/loops/list-open-cases-on-domain-review)** · base `serve-a-teams-open-cases`

- title: `feat(loo-6239): list open cases on domain review`
- body: the assessment panel shows why the team's domains can't send: each open case, who opened it, and the readings it points at.

sections.title: R1 and R2: settled
sections.body:
- **R1 is in the MVP**: every payload carries `v`, enforced by a CHECK.
- **R2 is accepted**: repeat causes dedupe against open cases from the first event; only a redelivery after release reopens. See the R2 lane.

sections.title: Keep content readings in the first PRs?
sections.body:
reading.reviewed, email scope and the publish effect are already built into the core branches. The alternative is cutting them out so the first PRs show only the core schema.

**Recommendation: keep them.** They're in the MVP lane already; cutting them out means a reshape for a smaller first diff, not a safer one.

sections.title: Readings retention on team delete
sections.body:
Events now outlive the team (plain `teamId`, no FK; purged by one line in `finalize-team-delete.ts` for now). Readings (`SuspiciousActivity`, `AccountLimitNotice`) are still deleted with the team, so a kept event could cite a reading that's gone.

**Recommendation: decide after the MVP.** While events are purged with the team too, nothing dangles. It becomes real the day that purge line is removed.

sections.title: team.deletion_requested as a case
sections.body:
This is R6 (condition cases): a case that should close when its condition clears, which rules can't do today.

**Recommendation: as planned, outside the MVP** (lane R6, flip → readers). It needs the ledger to be the authority first.

sections.title: The seed's CHECK exception
sections.body: **Not needed.** Adoption opens cases (`legacy.unrecorded`, decided by the rule `legacy.unrecorded@1`), and rules may write `opened` under `rules_open_or_review`. No guard is loosened.

sections.title: Restack: done
sections.body: All 39 branches are restacked on main `7afff5923c` (2026-11-04). 27 of the 34 above the MVP replayed with identical line changes; the flip branches were redone on top of the new record branches.
